behavior_constraints: Adding --strict-late-audit takes no value; passing --strict-late-audit=true is a usage error with exit 2
Supplying --strict-late-audit without --audit-log emits exactly 'ingest: --strict-late-audit requires --audit-log' on stderr and exits 2 with no output files created
Every late audit record's cutoff MUST be a JSON object with exactly two keys in order: {"value": "<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ>", "epoch_seconds": <int>}
cutoff.value must be 20-char strict RFC3339 UTC with Z suffix matching ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}Z$
cutoff.epoch_seconds is a bare JSON integer equal to Unix seconds for value; negative computed epoch clamps to {"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z", 0}

When --strict-late-audit is supplied, every late audit record gains watermark_lag_seconds (int, run-wide --watermark-lag value) and late_by_seconds (int, cutoff_epoch - event_ts_epoch, always positive) appended immediately after cutoff in that order
late record has 9 keys under --strict-late-audit in exact order: id, ts, type, shard, line, bucket, cutoff, watermark_lag_seconds, late_by_seconds
Without --strict-late-audit, late record has 7 keys with structured cutoff but no watermark_lag_seconds/late_by_seconds

--audit-log-digest emits new top-level block late_cutoff_stats positioned immediately after duplicate_reasons and immediately before resolved_against, always emitted regardless of flag or presence of late records
late_cutoff_stats has count, min_cutoff_epoch, max_cutoff_epoch as bare JSON integers; when count==0, min and max are 0
entities.summary: This round restructures every late audit record's cutoff into a {value, epoch_seconds} object, adds --strict-late-audit to expose watermark_lag_seconds and late_by_seconds, adds late_cutoff_stats to the audit digest, and (per intro) introduces --audit-log-rotate-bytes and --state-strict plus first_seen_epoch on pending_purchases.

# Structured Late Audit Cutoffs and Audit Log Rotation

Late audit records need to carry enough information for downstream tools to
reconstruct the watermark decision without guessing how a timestamp string was
formatted. The `cutoff` value in every `late` audit record is now a structured
